turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, bear with me, the computer is taking an age to open your record. Do sit down. What brings you in today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. I am quite all right, really. My wife thought I ought to come, though I should not like to waste a busy morning.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're not wasting it. One second, it's frozen on yesterday's clinic. There. What was she worried about?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): She says I am not myself. I have been sleeping poorly, and I have rather lost interest in things, though I am managing, I assure you.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Could you say that once more? Someone's printer has just started up behind me.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Of course. I am not sleeping well, and my energy is very low. I have lost interest in the garden, which I used to keep every evening.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the sleeping been off?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Some months, I should think. Um, since I left the firm. That was last winter, or, well, actually it may have been the winter before. I cannot be precise, I'm afraid.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Last winter or the one before. We'll not pin a date on it, then. You left the firm, was that redundancy?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I was accounts manager at Pellham Builders for twenty-two years. They released me when the contracts fell away. It was a considerable blow, though I prefer not to dwell.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm sorry. Right, I'm in your notes now, not the other chap's. Tell me what the nights are actually like.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): I do get off to sleep, then I wake near three and lie awake until morning. I had thought four hours, perhaps five on a kinder night.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Most nights, or only now and then?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Most nights. Well, actually, thinking of this past fortnight, it is nearer three hours than four. I do apologise for correcting myself.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Better to correct it. And the tiredness, is that all day?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I am drained by mid-morning. Even filling the kettle feels an effort on some days. I remain civil, naturally.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is the loss of interest only the garden?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No, it is wider than that. I have stopped following the cricket, and I no longer walk with my brother on a Sunday, which I used to enjoy very much.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about your appetite?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I still eat my meals, but there is little pleasure in them. I have not lost weight. My clothes fit just as they did.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any tears, or a sense of hopelessness?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not weep, Doctor. I would not call it hopeless. Flat, perhaps. The week seems to have very little colour in it.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am going to ask something directly, and I hope you will forgive it. Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself, or that you would be better off not here?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I have not, and I would not. I am quite clear there have been no thoughts of harming myself.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I am sorry if that was abrupt. The car park was full and I was a little flustered coming in. They have moved the ticket machine again.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the ticket machine? No, don't worry, I missed half of that, the screen flashed. You're here now, that's the main thing.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me see the medicines. The nurse typed this in at the desk earlier: ramipril five milligrams, once daily.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm afraid that is not right, Doctor. I take ten milligrams. They are the white tablets, one each morning.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ten, did you say, not five? The cursor jumped. Could you repeat it?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten milligrams of ramipril, every morning, for my blood pressure. I have been on that dose for a good while. I can bring the box if it helps.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please do bring the box next time. The high blood pressure is on your record, and I'll leave the ramipril dose queried, since the notes and what you're telling me don't agree.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines, or to anything else?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): None that I know of. I have always been able to take what is prescribed.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you drink, or smoke?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): A small whisky on a Sunday evening, and that is all. I have never smoked. My wife would not have it in the house in any case.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): And it's just the two of you at home?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. My wife is retired from teaching. She has been very patient with me, which I do appreciate.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm just going to feel your pulse while this page loads. It's 72, regular. You look weary, but you're neatly turned out, and I don't see any agitation.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. I did try to look respectable. One likes to make an effort for the surgery.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): From what you've described, I think this is a depressive episode, most likely tied to the redundancy. That's my working view, not a final label.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I also can't exclude a physical contribution, an underactive thyroid for example, until we have some bloods.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I understand. I would rather know, if there is something amiss in the blood.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll arrange a thyroid test, a full blood count, and kidney function, the last because of the ramipril. You can have them done this week. I'll book them.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): This week is perfectly acceptable. Thank you.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): On treatment, we could consider sertraline if things have not lifted in a few weeks. I am not starting any medicine for this today.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I would prefer that, Doctor. I should not like a new tablet just yet. If it is acceptable, I shall try to keep a steadier routine first.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Entirely acceptable. Same bedtime, up at the same time, and leave the phone out of the bedroom. The Sunday whisky is modest, I wouldn't fuss over that.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall do that. I have been reading the news on the telephone until midnight, which is a poor habit, I admit.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): That will be working against the sleep. I'll see you again in three weeks, with the blood results, and we'll revisit whether any tablet is needed.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. Yes, I can do that. Shall I book at the desk?

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, at reception on your way out. And if you feel worse before then, or if any thoughts of harming yourself did appear, come back sooner, or telephone the surgery the same day. Don't wait for the three weeks.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I shall. I do not expect that, but I will not ignore it if it happens. You have been very kind.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): One more thing, sorry, I've lost my place on the screen. The bloods, you were happy for this week?
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, this week is quite all right. And I shall bring the ramipril box so the dose can be settled.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Anything else you wanted to mention while I've got you?
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): No, thank you, Doctor. I think that covers it. I am grateful for your time.

spec.situation: Adult with poor sleep, low energy and loss of interest for months after a job loss or bereavement; partner or parent speaks for them; patient says 'I'm fine' then partly opens up; denies thoughts of self-harm clearly (doctor asks gently); medication discussed but not started today.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: High blood pressure supported, but ongoing status is from record/implication, not explicitly patient-stated.

omissions.text: Ramipril dose is stated by the patient as 10 mg every morning; the recorded medication entry omits the dose.
Sleep pattern detail: he can get off to sleep, then wakes near 3 a.m. and lies awake until morning.

No loss of appetite was effectively reported; he still eats his meals and has not lost weight, but there is little pleasure in eating. The recorded fact 'little pleasure in eating' should not imply reduced intake/appetite.
Patient reports no thoughts of harming himself and also denies feeling he would be better off not here; the latter part of the suicide-risk question is not recorded.
Doctor advised not just same bedtime and rising time and leaving the phone out of the bedroom, but specifically that reading news on the phone until midnight is likely worsening sleep.
Safety-net detail: if worse before the 3-week review, or if self-harm thoughts appear, he should come back sooner or telephone the surgery the same day and not wait for three weeks.
